script.spoken: TWA Flight 800 exploded shortly after take-off from New York. It broke apart and fell into the ocean, killing everyone aboard. Investigators traced the blast to the centre fuel tank. That tank was nearly empty. Heat from the air-conditioning units warmed the vapour inside. Warm fuel vapour is far easier to ignite than liquid fuel. A spark, most likely from wiring, set it off. New rules now require airliners to make those tanks far less flammable.
